Lebkuchen

Served at: First Sunday of Advent

Makes about 30 cookiesPrep 20 minCook 15 min

Lebkuchen is a traditional German spiced cookie enjoyed during the Advent season, especially on the First Sunday of Advent. These soft, aromatic cookies are often decorated with icing or chocolate and symbolize the festive spirit and anticipation of Christmas.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground allspice
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) honey
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) water
  • 1 large egg
  • 1/2 cup (50 g) chopped almonds
  • 1/4 cup (40 g) candied orange peel, finely chopped
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon lemon zest

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
  2. In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, nutmeg, allspice, and salt.
  3. In a small saucepan over low heat, combine honey, sugar, and water. Stir until sugar dissolves and mixture is warm but not boiling. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
  4. In a large bowl, beat the egg. Gradually add the warm honey mixture, vanilla extract, and lemon zest, mixing well.
  5. Slowly add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture, stirring until combined.
  6. Fold in the chopped almonds and candied orange peel.
  7. Using a tablespoon, drop rounded spoonfuls of dough onto the prepared baking sheets, spacing them about 2 inches (5 cm) apart.
  8. Bake for 12-15 minutes or until the cookies are firm but still soft in the center.
  9. Remove from oven and let cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
  10. Optionally, decorate with royal icing or dip half of each cookie in melted chocolate once cooled.

Tips

  • For a softer texture, store Lebkuchen in an airtight container with a slice of apple to keep them moist.
  • You can substitute candied orange peel with candied lemon peel or dried cranberries for a different flavor.
  • Allow the dough to rest overnight in the refrigerator for more developed flavors before baking.
